If you start with ice cream, adding cherries and hot fudge and whipped cream will make it taste great. But if you start with a bowl of meatballs . . . yuck! As traditional marketing fades away, the new tools seem irresistible. But they don't work as well for boring brands (meatballs?) that might still be profitable but don't attract word of mouth, such as Cheerios, Ford trucks, Barbie dolls or Budweiser. When Anheuser-Busch spends $40 million on an online network called BudTV, that's a meatball sundae. It leads to no new Bud drinkers, just a bad case of indigestion. 5 local restaurants switch up the meatball

Check out these five Central Jersey restaurants which are taking a twist to the classic meatball dish.

Jenna Intersimone
@JIntersimone
Updated Jan. 13, 2016, 12:38 p.m. ET
  
Nunzio's Kitchen uses their own 35-year-old meatball recipe.
* Alfonso's serves a "meatball sundae" as an appetizer.
* Luca's Ristorante has created meatballs that feature pine nuts and golden raisins.
The meatball is a classic staple: stacked on top of a helping of pasta and smothered in tomato sauce, no one can say no to the familiar comfort dish on a cold evening.
However, the basics of the meatball also grant the opportunity to switch up time-tried recipes and create something entirely new.

I’ll never forget the day I heard someone in my department (h/t to Patrick M) said “meatball sundae” and I had no clue what it meant.
If you visualize a meatball sundae, it’s actually very simple. Would you put cold ice cream or ice cream toppings on hot meatballs? In the end, the toppings or ice cream melts and you’re left with melted ice cream on cold meatballs. It’s a great visual, right? It’s better to start with an ice cream base and add your toppings.
